chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:'

Verily, when Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, wants to take account of the believer, He gives him his book in his right hand, and His reckoning is between Him and him privately. He says, 'My servant, did you do such and such, and perform such and such?' He says, 'Yes, my Lord, I have done that.' He says, 'I have forgiven it for you and replaced it with good deeds.' The people say, 'Glory be to Allah! Did this servant not have even a single evil deed?'
As for the one who is given his record in his right hand, he will have an easy reckoning, and will return to his people well pleased.
I asked, 'Who are his people?' He said, 'His people in the world are his people in Paradise, if they were believers.'
And if He wishes ill for His servant, He calls him to account in front of all the people, reproves him, and gives him his book in his left hand.
And as for the one who is given his record from behind his back, he will cry for destruction and will burn in a blazing fire. He used to live among his people well pleased.
I asked, 'Which people?' He replied, 'His people in the world.'
I asked, '[What is the meaning of] His statement: He thought he would never return?' He said, 'He assumed that he would never return.'
ai.seo_question: How does Allah's private reckoning for believers differ from public reckoning for sinners?
ai.summary: This hadith elucidates the distinction between the 'easy reckoning' (hisab yasir) for the righteous and the public accounting for the wicked, emphasizing that private divine forgiveness preserves the believer's honor before the community. It further clarifies the theological nuance of 'his family' (ahluhu) in the Quranic verses, interpreting it as the worldly family for the sinner and the spiritual family in Paradise for the believer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the continuity of faith-based relationships. The narration underscores the mercy of Allah in concealing the sins of the faithful while exposing the negligence of those who presumed they would not be resurrected.
